Article Title: Oil prices dip marginally as US weighs easing sanctions on ‘shadow fleet’ tankers
Article Text:
Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel

Oil prices fell slightly on Friday as investors weighed rising tensions in the Middle East against the possibility of the US easing restrictions on ships carrying oil from sanctioned countries. Brent crude stood at $105.40, a decline of 0.52% while WTI crude was trading at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%.The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. WTI settled more than 3% higher on Thursday, supported by a significant reduction in US crude inventories. Brent, however, finished the session with little change.Efforts to increase supplies have also failed to fully ease market concerns. On Thursday, the International Energy Agency agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel, alongside any oil left over from the record emergency reserve release announced in March. The move was intended to increase availability and bring down soaring prices.Another major factor under consideration is a possible change in US sanctions policy. The Trump administration is discussing whether to lift restrictions on certain vessels in the so-called “shadow fleet”, which has carried oil and petroleum products from Russia, Iran and Venezuela, a US official said on Wednesday, as cited by Reuters.The proposed step is aimed at easing record-high global freight rates.The deliberations follow US President Donald Trump’s temporary lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel fuel. The decision prompted criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some Republicans in the US Senate.Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market. The intensifying conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis, along with fresh attacks on ships in the region, has provided support to oil prices.Attacks around the waterway have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and stricter sanctions imposed last month.The violence also spread to Yemen’s southern city of Aden on Thursday, when the Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex, killing two guards. Separately, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure as the conflict continued to escalate.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $105.40 per barrel on Friday, a decline of 0.52%. WTI crude was at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%. The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market.

Article Title: India raises petrol export duty fivefold to Rs 2.5/litre, cuts diesel levy to Rs 8.5
Article Text:
Govt raises petrol export duty, cuts diesel levy

NEW DELHI: The government has raised the export duty on petrol fivefold to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5, while cutting the levy on diesel to Rs 8.5 per litre from Rs 16. The revised rates came into effect on October 16.The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre, according to a finance ministry notification issued on Friday.The revised rates cover the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), with no road and infrastructure cess (RIC) applicable on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF. The changes follow the previous revision, which took effect on October 1.Export duties on the three petroleum products are reviewed every fortnight, with rates determined by average international prices of crude oil and the respective fuels during the period since the last review. The latest revision changes the levies on petrol and diesel in opposite directions, while leaving the ATF duty unchanged.The revised export duties will not affect the existing excise duty rates on petrol and diesel sold for domestic consumption.India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026 as crude oil prices surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran.The tax was intended to discourage exports and protect domestic supplies of petroleum products amid the conflict in the Middle East. It was also aimed at preventing exporters from benefiting unduly from differences between domestic and international prices as global crude oil prices rose.The government imposed export duties on diesel and ATF on March 27, 2026, and introduced the levy on petrol exports from May 16. Rates have since been reviewed every fortnight.
Article Summary: The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre. India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026.

Article Title: India-China trade jumps 29% to $91.76 billion, overtakes US in first half of FY27
Article Text:
Representative image (India-China trade rebounds as New Delhi looks to rebuild bilateral ties)

India-US trade rises, but surplus narrows

India looks to rebuild trade ties with China

Exports rise across markets in first half of FY27

India’s bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion in April-September 2026-27, making Beijing India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the financial year, according to commerce ministry data.Two-way trade between India and China stood at $71.24 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.China moved ahead of the US, with India’s trade with Washington rising 16.5 per cent to $83.14 billion during the first six months of the current fiscal year, compared with $71.39 billion a year earlier.India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period. Imports from China grew 27.82 per cent to $80.34 billion, against $62.86 billion previously.The faster growth in imports widened India’s trade deficit with China to $68.93 billion in the first half of FY27, from $54.06 billion in the corresponding period last year, the data showed.India’s bilateral trade with the US increased to $83.14 billion in April-September 2026-27 from $71.39 billion in the year-ago period.Exports to the US rose 11.11 per cent to $50.81 billion from $45.73 billion, while imports increased 25.98 per cent to $32.32 billion from $25.66 billion, according to the commerce ministry data.As imports grew faster than exports, India’s trade surplus with the US narrowed to $18.49 billion from $20.07 billion in the first half of 2025-26.Despite tariff-related disruptions, the US remained India’s largest merchandise export destination during the period. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction and that both sides were working to conclude it at the earliest.“The negotiations are in the right direction. Probably, we are in a very good zone. We anticipate closing the deal and signing it at the earliest possible time,” Agrawal said.He said the agreement would depend on the finalisation of the broader US tariff framework, with a parallel process underway under Section 301. India is seeking preferential access to the American market to help its exporters compete with those from other countries, he added.The increase in trade with China comes as New Delhi signals efforts to improve bilateral relations. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday that India was working to rebuild its relationship with China, but the last word on the process had not yet been scripted.Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal also said the two countries were in contact on trade-related issues.“There are discussions going on on both sides on trade issues also...constant discussions will help improve the trade ties between the two countries,” he told reporters, according to news agency PTI.The commerce ministry data also showed substantial changes in India’s trade with other countries during April-September 2026-27.Exports to Singapore rose 103 per cent, while shipments to Tanzania increased 122.5 per cent. However, exports to the UAE, the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia declined.On the imports side, inbound shipments from Oman rose 210.9 per cent, while imports from Brazil increased sharply, with the data citing a rise of 143.13 per cent. Imports from the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Switzerland declined.Separately, India’s merchandise exports rose 23.04 per cent year-on-year to $44.4 billion in September, while imports increased 8 per cent to $74.61 billion, according to government data.The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion in September from $33 billion a year earlier, although it widened from $26.86 billion in August.Cumulatively, merchandise exports rose 18.51 per cent to $259.89 billion during April-September 2026-27, while imports increased 16.31 per cent to $437.53 billion. The trade deficit for the first half of the fiscal year widened to $177.64 billion from $156.88 billion in the corresponding period of 2025-26.Agrawal said exports were maintaining their growth trend and expressed hope that merchandise exports could exceed $500 billion if the momentum continued. India’s merchandise exports stood at $442 billion in 2025-26.
Article Summary: Bilateral trade with China rose nearly 29 per cent year-on-year to $91.76 billion. India’s exports to China increased 36 per cent to $11.41 billion during April-September, from $8.38 billion in the year-ago period.

Article Title: Elon Musk's monopoly charge, Reliance's response: What's the Starlink-Jio row all about?
Article Text:
Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink

Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry

Government asks Starlink to comply with law

NEW DELHI: Reliance Industries has welcomed Elon Musk ’s Starlink to India, saying it has never feared competition and that its own satellite services are also in the queue.The statement comes as a response to Musk’s repeated allegations that vested interests were obstructing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.In a statement released on Friday, the company said India’s investment and innovation landscape was open to both domestic and foreign players, with the same regulatory process applying to all applicants.The statement, posted on social media platform X, stated, “In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio 's own satellite services await clearances.”The telecom firm further added, “At Reliance, we have never feared competition.We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”Reliance’s statement came after SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk accused the Indian conglomerate of benefiting from the existing market structure and alleged that arguments against Starlink’s entry were contradictory.In a post on X, Musk had said, "The ridiculous arguments by Ambani’s army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole."Musk argued that greater competition would give Indian consumers more choices, even if it reduced the profits of existing players. However, he said, this would not necessarily threaten their businesses."The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," he wrote.Musk had previously alleged monopolistic practices in India’s telecommunications market and questioned the regulatory barriers facing Starlink’s commercial launch in the country.In another post, he directly addressed the government, writing, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?"The government has denied Musk’s allegation that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said that there is no question of allowing a monopoly in satellite communications. He also said three entities are in line for final approval for commercial licences.Scindia said that India was close to taking a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services. All licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before beginning commercial operations.Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch its services in India because it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to establish domestic infrastructure, a senior government official said earlier this week.The government has no objection to the company rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations, sources said.A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the “first hop”, connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to establish base stations is intended to help authorities ensure compliance with the law.Reliance Jio, Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Musk’s Starlink are the three entities planning to launch satellite communication services in India.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal has also said that Airtel’s satellite venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, could receive regulatory approval before Starlink because it applied earlier and is further along in the process.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani owned Reliance responds to allegations involving Musk's Starlink. Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.

Article Title: Rs 1 crore-plus salaries: Amid layoffs, which Indian IT sector jobs are getting huge salary premiums?
Article Text:
Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior.

Even as restructuring and layoffs happen, some jobs in the IT sector are getting paid well - and across levels whether entry or senior. Which roles are in demand? What are the average salary levels for special capability sets and which roles are under pressure?

What are the salary levels for those getting hired at premiums?

AI’s Role Disruption Map

Entry level salaries

The report lists annual salaries of Rs 1.08 crore for AI Architects, Rs 1.02 crore for Industrial Data Architects and Rs 95.8 lakh for OT Security Architects. These figures reflect the value that is being placed on designing, securing and governing complex technology systems, beyond coding alone.

Entry-level salaries for Tier 2 AI-Adjacent

Entry level salaries for Tier 3 AI-Support

So, what can IT sector professionals do?

At the entry level, he says professionals with strong foundations in software engineering, data and AI application can distinguish themselves through practical implementation skills.

At the mid-career level, expertise in areas such as AI engineering, machine learning operations and enterprise AI integration becomes particularly valuable as organisations look to move beyond experimentation towards deployment at scale.

At the senior level, compensation increasingly reflects the ability to architect enterprise AI systems, lead transformation programmes and ensure that technology investments deliver measurable business outcomes, he adds.

Early and Mid Career Salary Trends Across Roles

Biggest takeaway

For early-career professionals, this means building strong technical fundamentals while gaining hands-on experience in AI, data and cloud technologies.

For mid-career professionals, the priority is to move beyond execution and develop the ability to integrate technologies, improve workflows and translate domain expertise into scalable solutions.

For senior professionals, the focus must extend to strategic decision-making, enterprise-wide AI adoption, governance and the ability to connect technology investments with business performance, he says.

AI capability maturity framework: From skills to salary premiums

Till a few years ago, software engineers in India were commanding high salary premiums and the IT sector was a reliable source of employment. While still employing lakhs, the artificial intelligence-led disruptions have meant that there is growing uncertainty on the relevance of traditional IT sector roles.As Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital says, “Every few years, the labour market crosses a threshold that is easy to miss in the moment and impossible to reverse in hindsight. India's digital workforce crossed one this year.”“This landscape brings immense opportunity, but it also collapses old certainties about how talent is valued. Job titles and role definitions are becoming less reliable indicators of capability or compensation,” she says.The fundamental point to understand is that India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill-differentiated compensation; with specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable.According to a TeamLease Digital report on Digital Skills and Salary Primer FY2026-27, there is a widening pay gap in India’s technology sector, with premiums increasingly going to professionals who can build, integrate, secure and manage AI systems. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.The premium concentrates in four families, AI, Data, Cloud and Cybersecurity, and peaks where capability depth meets governance and scale.And, this divide is visible across AI skill tiers. For example, the report puts entry-level median pay for AI-core roles at Rs 13.2 lakh, compared with Rs 9-10.2 lakh for AI-adjacent roles and Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh for AI-support roles. The projected salary growth is 16-21% for AI-core, against 13-18% for AI-adjacent and 7-8% for AI-support.Not only that, the premiums also extend to architecture, data and cybersecurity. The report says that skills such as GenAI engineers, AI architects, ML platform and cloud security are the highest in demand.“The 108.6 LPA figure is the median for AI Architects with 15+ years in our analysis of 37,000 roles. It reflects a senior role, not a market-wide norm. The differentiator is the ability to own architecture, scale production systems, manage risk, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes,” explains Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital.Also, geographies no longer define premiums as much. For example, according to the report, a GenAI engineer in Indore earns around Rs 16.5 lakh per annum, and out-earns cybersecurity talent in Bengaluru that gets Rs 14.4 lakh.Milind Shah, Managing Director, Randstad Digital - India tells TOI that the compensation for niche AI roles can vary considerably depending on the depth of expertise, role complexity and business impact. On an average, talent with niche tech skills may command anywhere between a 10-25% premium.Why are these roles commanding a premium? It’s a mix of skill shortage and the roles themselves generating more business value that routine IT jobs no longer are.According to Neeti Sharma, only about 16% of India’s IT professionals hold AI skills, so the supply is thin. She explains that companies are not able to find people who can take AI from pilot to production and stand accountable for it.“But this is not wage inflation. The market is pricing roles whose output is the AI system itself, which makes them the hardest to substitute. Routine support keeps operations running, and that is the layer AI is compressing first. Employers are paying for scarcity, and for people who can own the outcome,” she tells TOI.Reskilling is central to the shift. The TeamLease report points to pathways such as moving testers into intelligent operations, analysts into decision intelligence, and mid-career professionals into platform, product, governance and architecture roles.Its broader message is that combining core technical expertise with AI skills, domain knowledge and business judgement will increasingly determine salary growth.Milind Shah shares strategies for every level:So, what does this mean for tech professionals? The biggest takeaway is that professionals need to shift from being defined by the roles they perform to the capabilities they bring to the business.“As AI becomes embedded across technology functions, the value of talent will increasingly depend on the ability to adapt, solve complex problems and apply emerging technologies to real-world business challenges,” Milind Shah says.For people who are in traditional IT sector roles, it’s important to understand that while the jobs are not disappearing, routine execution roles are reducing.Repetitive reporting, manual testing, basic operational support and rule-based processing face pressure as AI and automation reshape work. The report does not suggest that all these jobs will disappear; rather, salary growth may slow unless workers move towards higher-value responsibilities.“Those in repetitive reporting, manual testing, and basic support are most exposed. The route up is adjacency, not reinvention: a BI analyst into data engineering, a sysadmin into cloud, a QA or IAM specialist into security and governance. Pair one technical skill with deep sector knowledge, and keep proof of work that moves a business outcome,” Neeti Sharma says.Not only that, this shift also has implications for how professionals approach career development.So if you are planning to upskill to keep yourself relevant, understand that it should not be driven solely by the popularity of a technology or the prospect of a higher salary.“Instead, employees should identify the capabilities emerging as critical within their industry, understand how these capabilities address business needs and build demonstrable expertise through practical application,” Milind Shah advises.
Article Summary: India’s technology talent market is witnessing a shift towards skill- differentiated compensation. Specialised capabilities in AI, machine learning, cloud engineering and data science becoming increasingly valuable. Routine, execution-led roles are facing greater salary pressure, while specialised skills are becoming more valuable.

Article Title: Trump waives Russia sanctions, restrictions and duties under Graham Act
Article Text:
Diesel prices have become a growing political concern ahead of the November 3 midterm elections

US President Donald Trump has waived several sanctions, restrictions and duties targeting Russia under the Graham Act, just weeks after signing the legislation aimed at squeezing Moscow over its invasion of Ukraine. The move comes as his administration seeks to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November’s midterm elections.In an executive order issued on Saturday, Trump invoked a provision of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 that allows the president to waive its measures in the national interest. He said he had submitted the required certification and a report explaining the basis for the decision to Congress.The order waives duties provided for under Sections 112 and 113 of the Act, sanctions and restrictions under Section 102(d), and several other provisions covering sanctions against foreign persons and restrictions on individuals. The waivers will remain in effect until Trump or the secretary of state, in consultation with other officials where appropriate, determines that further action is necessary.The move follows Trump's announcement that the US would purchase Russian diesel after he held what he described as a “highly successful discussion” with Russian President Vladimir Putin.Trump said Moscow had agreed to supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by additional shipments in November and subsequent months.“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump said on Truth Social.The US president added that lowering fuel costs for Americans, particularly farmers, ranchers and truckers, was his “Greatest Priority”.Diesel prices have become a growing political concern ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Prices reached a record $6.52 a gallon in September and were around $6.28 on Friday, putting pressure on businesses and consumers.Under the executive order, the US Trade Representative, in consultation with other senior officials, will monitor countries' purchases of Russian crude oil and natural gas, as well as efforts to evade sanctions, and report developments to the president. The order also provides for additional duties of 500% on Russian goods, subject to specified exceptions and waivers, and 100% on goods from certain major importers of Russian energy and facilitators of sanctions evasion.The shift also comes after Washington repeatedly pressured India to curb its purchases of Russian energy, using tariff threats to push New Delhi to reduce its reliance on Moscow.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has waived several sanctions, restrictions and duties targeting Russia under the Graham Act. The move comes as his administration seeks to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November’s midterm elections. The waivers will remain in effect until Trump or the secretary of state determines that further action is necessary.

Article Title: Reliance Industries to Elon Musk: Competition welcome, but follow rules
Article Text:
At Reliance, we have never feared competition, the company said

New Delhi: Ahead of its Rs 30,213-crore Jio IPO, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk ’s tirade on X and said it welcomed competition.Last Wednesday, Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of “blocking” Starlink’s entry into India before naming Ambani over the next two days in a series of posts.In an early morning statement on Friday, Reliance Industries said: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”“At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India’s crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just 10 years, Jio has earned the trust of over 53 crore customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world,” the statement said.It added: “Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign.Jio’s own satellite services await clearances.”Govt had also denied Musk’s charges. Last Thursday, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia had said at India Mobile Congress: “There is a lot of conversation about a particular party (Starlink). But there are three parties that have got licences… As and when govt decides the charge system on revenue basis, spectrum will be assigned to them and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, then they can start operations. ”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Musk’s Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service here so that even remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. Jeff Bezos’s Amazon’s Project Kuiper is eying a licence to do so.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk ’s tirade on X and said it welcomed competition. “At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best,” the company said.

Article Title: 'Ready to connect India with high-speed internet': Starlink reacts to Reliance's message
Article Text:
Starlink says it is ready to bring high-speed internet to India, after Reliance welcomed competition in satellite communications amid Elon Musk’s allegations of obstruction.

NEW DELHI: Starlink has said it is ready to connect India with high-speed internet, responding to Reliance Industries ’ statement that it welcomes competition in satellite communications, provided all players follow Indian laws and policies.“We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely - and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet,” the company said in a post on X.The response after Reliance Industries pushed back against Elon Musk’s allegations that certain business groups were blocking Starlink’s entry into India.Reliance said it welcomed competition and that every player, including Jio, must comply with the country’s laws and policies. It also noted that Jio’s own satellite services were awaiting clearances."In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record.Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people.That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances," Reliance had said.Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of blocking Starlink’s entry into India before naming Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani in a series of posts.The government has also rejected Musk’s claims. Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said satellite spectrum would be assigned once the government finalised the revenue-sharing framework and companies met security requirements.Starlink, Reliance Jio and Eutelsat OneWeb have received licences to provide satellite communication services in India. The services are expected to extend internet connectivity to remote areas where laying conventional broadband infrastructure is difficult. Amazon’s Project Kuiper is also seeking a licence.
Article Summary: Starlink says it is ready to connect India with high-speed internet. Response after Reliance Industries pushed back against Elon Musk’s allegations of obstruction. Reliance said it welcomed competition and that every player, including Jio, must comply with the country's laws and policies.

Article Title: Trade imbalance with China growing due to barriers: FM Sitharaman
Article Text:
She, however, insisted that dialogue is the best way to address these issues

NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Friday flagged her concerns over the large — and exponentially growing — trade imbalance with China and said Beijing has not addressed India’s concerns for nearly a decade and continued to deploy non-tariff barriers.“The trade imbalance is something we have been talking with China for several years, we are denied market access even for those goods where there are immense market opportunities in China. We are global leaders in generic drugs, bovine meat, vegetables and perishables, which has huge potential in China. A decade has gone consistently putting a case for market access for Indian products. Non-tariff barriers have been very strong and China uses them unhesitatingly, whether it is in the name of phytosanitary measures or any other for which due investigations can happen, for which both sides can sit and talk but no progress is made. Non-tariff barriers are the biggest worry in trade between India and China,” she said during an interaction organised by the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meeting in Bangkok.She, however, insisted that dialogue is the best way to address these issues. “The global approach of countries imposing tariffs to correct the imbalance has never been taken by us. India doesn’t believe in that approach.We sit and talk, it is very tiresome, but we follow that approach, rather than put countervailing duties (against subsidies) or some to counter non-tariff barriers on the other side.”The minister said that India believed in multilateralism but was entering into bilateral trade deals to deal with the current global environment, which has seen a spurt in the use of barriers. "Rapidly, we have to connect with many parts of the world for which negotiations have been going on for a very long time. Countries with which we spent a long-time negotiating have realised that the sooner we tie up on our bilateral relationship, we will be benefiting our people because of the movement of goods and services which will bring in that lubrication at a time when world is in a very difficult position. So, trade negotiations are being conducted quickly, although they have not been easy.”While flagging high prices impacting India’s import bill for crude and fertiliser, the FM said the Indian economy was robust. “Much against all odds, India is able to keep up the growth. It has been the fastest-growing economy for last five-six years, since Covid. Being inclusive and ensuring that everyone has access to resources and skilling and making sure that fiscal prudence is not lost, have helped. More importantly, public spending on capex has helped build infra in the country, which has a greater multiplier effect,” she said.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Friday flagged her concerns over the large — and exponentially growing — trade imbalance with China. She said Beijing has not addressed India’s concerns for nearly a decade and continued to deploy non- tariff barriers. But she insisted that dialogue is the best way to address these issues.

Article Title: ‘Much appreciated:’ Musk on Reliance Starlink stand as Rubio set to meet Ambani
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Elon Musk ’s blow hot and cold stand for getting Starlink access to India has now entered a conciliatory phase after the tech trillionaire was all fire on X last week. The change in tone comes at a time when US secretary of state Marco Rubio is in India and will visit the world’s largest oil refinery in Jamnagar that’s owned by Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani — who was targeted by Musk last week.“Much appreciated,” Musk said on X late Friday night in response to Reliance Industries first reply to his charges on Friday, where Mukesh Ambani’s conglomerate had said: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must… abide by the laws and policies of the land…. As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances.”Starlink also responded to Reliance post, saying it has “worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for five plus years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet.”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Musk’s Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service here so that even remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. Billionaire Jeff Bezos-led Amazon's Project Kuiper is eying a licence to do so.Starlink clearance is being seen as part of the larger Indo-US ties with several factors being part of the play including the trade deal and threat of tariffs over buying Russian oil.Sunil Bharti Mittal had this Wednesday said the company was significantly ahead of Starlink in securing approvals for satellite communications services in India. “We are already waiting for approvals, I am significantly ahead, we got our approvals five years back, so I will be happy to get my approvals a few days before it (Starlink),” Mittal had said at an event.Reliance Jio has proposed a constellation of around 1,600 Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites and 23 ground stations to provide sovereign satellite internet connectivity across India.Last Wednesday, Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of “blocking” Starlink’s entry to India without naming anyone but saying “you can guess who they are” and then named Ambani over the next two days in a series of X posts.
Article Summary: Starlink also responded to Reliance post, saying it has “worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for five plus years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic.”

Article Title: IDBI Bank disinvestment: Govt clarifies shareholding concerns, says 2003 law does not restrict stake dilution
Article Text:
Government clarifies concerns surrounding selling of IDBI stake

Budget speeches on IDBI disinvestment

NEW DELHI: The finance ministry on Saturday clarified that the government’s power to dilute its stake in IDBI Bank was not restricted by the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. The statement comes amid media reports on the 2003 legislative developments concerning the government’s shareholding in the bank.The ministry said that an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of the government’s stake was moved during the Union Budget 2003 discussions and parliamentary debate on the Act, but was rejected and did not become part of the enacted legislation.The ministry cited the Delhi High Court’s December 17, 2018, judgment in All India IDBI Officers’ Association vs. Union of India and Others, which dismissed a petition challenging the government’s decision to dilute its shareholding.In paragraph 41, the court held, “This Court is of the view that the statements made before the House almost 15 years earlier, in a debate relating to a legislative activity, would not preclude the Central Government from diluting its stake in IDBI Ltd. Indisputably, the legislation enacted by the Parliament after the debate did not contain the amendment that was sought to be introduced. The statements made before the House cannot substitute or override the statue so enacted by the Parliament.Paragraph 42 stated, “There is no ambiguity in the language of the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003 and there is no scope to read any provision into the said enactment which proscribes the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd.”The government said the ruling clarified that the doctrine of promissory estoppel could not be invoked to prevent it from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Bank.“The aforesaid judgment is significant as it specifically addresses the doctrine of promissory estoppel, which was relied upon in challenging the Government’s decision to dilute its shareholding. The doctrine could not be invoked to prevent the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd,” the official statement said.The ministry also cited Budget announcements tracing the government’s disinvestment policy. In his 2016–17 Budget speech, then finance minister Arun Jaitley said, “Our Public Sector Banks will have to be strong and competitive. The Bank Board Bureau will be operationalised during 2016-17 and a roadmap for consolidation of Public Sector Banks will be spelt out.The process of transformation of IDBI Bank has already started. Government will take it forward and also consider the option of reducing its stake to below 50%.”In the 2021–22 Budget, then finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman listed IDBI Bank among transactions targeted for completion during the year.She said, “In spite of COVID-19, we have kept working towards strategic disinvestment. A number of transactions namely BPCL, Air India, Shipping Corporation of India, Container Corporation of India, IDBI Bank, BEML, Pawan Hans, Neelachal Ispat Nigam limited among others would be completed in 2021-22. Other than IDBI Bank, we propose to take up the privatization of two Public Sector Banks and one General Insurance company in the year 2021-22. This would require legislative amendments and I propose to introduce the amendments in this Session itself.”
Article Summary: Government clarifies concerns surrounding selling of IDBI stake. An amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of the government’s stake was moved during the Union Budget 2003 discussions and parliamentary debate on the Act, but was rejected and did not become part of the enacted legislation.

Article Title: Stellantis to invest Rs 4k crore, plans 12 Jeep, Citroën models
Article Text:
India will also become a larger global manufacturing and export hub, with Stellantis planning to produce left-hand-drive vehicles locally for overseas markets, expanding its reach to more than 50 countries.

:

TOI

NEW DELHIAutomaker Stellantis plans to invest another Rs 4,000 crore in India over three years, starting 2027 as it looks to revive the fortunes of its Jeep and Citroën brands through new products, greater localisation and multiple powertrain options, including hybrids and electric vehicles.Under its FaSTLAne 2030 strategy, the company will introduce 12 products, comprising seven all-new models and five refreshed offerings. The first launch is scheduled for the second quarter of 2027.Stellantis India CEO and MD Shailesh Hazela toldthat the company expects to triple its current market share, banking on a stronger product portfolio and improved affordability.Acknowledging that Jeep and Citroën have struggled to achieve significant volumes, Hazela said greater localisation would be central to improving competitiveness. The company also plans to leverage its existing partnership with Tata Motors and local supplier networks to reduce costs and strengthen manufacturing capabilities.“We will apply this learning to Jeep through greater localisation, so that the cost of ownership comes down and the product becomes more accessible to customers,” he said, adding that Citroën has achieved 90% localisation.On electrification, Hazela said Stellantis would offer conventional engines, hybrids and EVs across its portfolio. “We will give customers choices across segments and be ready to respond to demand based on their preferences,” he said.India will also become a larger global manufacturing and export hub, with Stellantis planning to produce left-hand-drive vehicles locally for overseas markets, expanding its reach to more than 50 countries.
Article Summary: Under its FaSTLAne 2030 strategy, the company will introduce 12 products, comprising seven all-new models and five refreshed offerings. The first launch is scheduled for the second quarter of 2027. India will also become a larger global manufacturing and export hub, with Stellantis planning to produce left- hand-drive vehicles.

Article Title: As price hikes weigh, EMIs take centrestage
Article Text:
On Amazon, for example, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year (Representative image)

MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales seem to be missing their fiery spark this year. Price hikes have weighed on smartphone sales volumes, typically the biggest driver of the season with final prices in many cases higher than last year even after discounts.Price increases have also made durables costlier with the share of large-ticket purchases (overall) through EMIs having significantly gone up this year. On Amazon, for example, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year, said Aman Deep Lohan, director, home, kitchen and outdoors at Amazon India.Amid inflationary pressures and shrinking household budgets, smaller-ticket items found more space in shopping carts with consumers prioritising value for money. At the end of a week’s sales, average order values (AOV) are lower with growth having been led by categories such as fashion, beauty, home and general merchandise.“Value commerce, which covers items priced below Rs 500, handled about half of all festive orders. AOVs are 7-8% lower than last year because the basket moved to lower-ticket categories and channels. By value, phones and electronics still lead; by growth, softlines lead,” said Nikhil Dalal, associate partner, Redseer Strategy Consultants, which captured data from Oct 8-12.On Flipkart, about 7 in 10 units sold were priced under Rs 500.Unlike other seasons when a major chunk of the sales happen during Navaratri (the first leg of sale), analysts expect sales this year to be more spread out through Diwali as consumers strike a balance between their pockets and desire to buy. Estimates from Datum Intelligence showed that sales dropped by about 7-10% in the first four opening days to Rs 29,800-30,900 crore. “Last year’s sales opened on Sept 22, the day the GST rate cuts took effect. This year’s opening had no such trigger,” analysts at the firm said.As price hikes shrunk the quantum of discounts on offer, particularly in demand-heavy categories such as smartphones, consumers went bigger on EMIs to buy premium products. “Phones entered the sale with average prices about 15% higher than a year ago. So even a similar headline discount leaves the final price above last year’s festive price.“Across devices, sale-day prices were only about 5% to 10% below pre-sale levels, depending on category. Discounts were deeper where inventory and competition allowed,” Dalal said.
Article Summary: India’s online festive sales seem to be missing their fiery spark this year. Price hikes have weighed on smartphone sales volumes. On Amazon, for example, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year.

Article Title: From stop-gap to in-command, IDBI’s Rakesh Sharma stays the course
Article Text:
He oversaw the turnaround, which included govt pumping in around Rs 25,000 crore between 2010 and 2020, as well insolvency law-driven clean-up

NEW DELHI: Rakesh Sharma, the low-profile managing director and CEO of IDBI Bank, who will lead the transition at the once formidable development financial institution, will go down as one of the longest serving bank CEOs.For someone who would have been disappointed at not making the cut as SBI’s deputy managing director has gone on to lead three lenders for over 12 years, and counting. On Thursday, Fairfax announced that Sharma will continue to helm the bank with former ICICI Prudential Life MD NS Kannan to be designated as the new chairman. During an analyst call, Fairfax chairman Prem Watsa also named former HDFC chairman Deepak Parekh, former CSB Bank CEO Rajendran CVR and former HDFC Bank deputy MD Paresh Sukthankar as advisers.Sharma’s appointment came as a surprise to several within IDBI Bank as he had been sent to the Mumbai-headquartered outfit as a stop gap CEO with the Centre hoping to move ahead with its plan to privatise the bank. After quitting SBI as chief general manager, Sharma became the MD & CEO of Lakshmi Vilas Bank in March 2014 and then went on to lead Canara Bank from Sept 2015 to July 2018 after govt decided to rope in talent from the private sector.Sharma took charge when IDBI Bank had hit a low and was the first lender to be part of RBI’s prompt corrective action framework in May 2017 due to poor asset quality, low capital and mounting losses, resulting in restrictions. He oversaw the turnaround, which included govt pumping in around Rs 25,000 crore between 2010 and 2020, as well insolvency law-driven clean-up.
Article Summary: Rakesh Sharma will continue to helm the bank with former ICICI Prudential Life MD NS Kannan to be designated as the new chairman. Sharma’s appointment came as a surprise to several within IDBI Bank as he had been sent to the Mumbai- headquartered outfit as a stop gap CEO.

Article Title: AI agents accessing corp data undetected: CERT-In
Article Text:
CERT-In reported that AI models undergoing testing accessed an unnamed Indian company's confidential data and live systems without authorization

NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are emerging as a serious cybersecurity threat to Indian organisations, accessing sensitive corporate data without authorisation and exploiting existing security gaps at speeds that leave companies with little time to respond, cybersecurity experts have warned.The concerns follow a critical advisory issued on Thursday by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), which revealed that AI agents being tested by technology companies had accessed live systems of Indian organisations, reading business records, personal information and confidential data. None of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access, with incidents coming to light through disclosures by AI model providers.CERT-In also flagged financially motivated cyberattacks involving publicly available AI tools that have reduced the time between initial intrusion and damage from days to just hours.Jaydeep Singh, general manager, India, Kaspersky, said conventional cybersecurity measures were struggling to address threats posed by autonomous systems operating with legitimate credentials.“The risk is real and growing. To be useful, AI agents are often connected to emails, code repositories and cloud systems, which gives them access to far more data than a typical user would need,” Singh said.The advisory identified exposed credentials, poorly secured application programming interfaces (APIs), excessive cloud permissions and weak authentication as vulnerabilities being exploited by AI agents.Sunil Sharma, managing director and VP-sales, India and SAARC, Sophos, said the growing autonomy of these systems was complicating detection.“AI agents can access data, invoke APIs and interact with internal systems autonomously, creating risks when permissions exceed their intended purpose or access controls are inadequate,” Sharma said.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are emerging as a serious cybersecurity threat to Indian organisations. They are accessing sensitive corporate data without authorisation and exploiting existing security gaps. Concerns follow a critical advisory issued on Thursday by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)

Article Title: Tech stocks power Sensex to best week in 6 months
Article Text:
The Nifty 50 rose 2.8% to 23,146 and sensex added 3.1% to 74,729

Indian share benchmarks posted their best weekly performance in six months on Friday, powered by a rally in IT stocks after stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and a selloff in global AI markets that prompted value-buying elsewhere.Investors now await results from several heavyweight companies, including major banks, and the IPO of Jio Platforms. The Nifty 50 rose 2.8% to 23,146 and sensex added 3.1% to 74,729, marking their strongest weekly showing since April 10. On the day, the indexes gained 0.7% and 0.6%, respectively. MSCI’s broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan fell 5.8% this week.“The absence of any major negative surprises from IT earnings, coupled with management commentary pointing to growing AI-led revenue, has given investors confidence to return to these beaten-down names,” said Saurabh Jain, deputy VP of equities at SMC Global. “That rebound in IT has, in turn, lifted the benchmarks.”The IT index surged 3.9% on Friday, taking its weekly gain to 11.7%, its steepest such advance in 18 years.TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra climbed between 13.4% and 18.2%, placing them among the Nifty 50’s top weekly percentage gainers. Near-term direction will hinge on results from ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank, due on Saturday, Jain said, adding “the market, and IT shares in particular, could pause next week as the Jio Platforms IPO absorbs liquidity.”Meanwhile, the rupee strengthened by 10 paise to regain 94 levels closingat 94.96. It was buoyed by Reserve Bank of India’s policy measures aimed at boosting the currency.
Article Summary: The Nifty 50 rose 2.8% to 23,146 and sensex added 3.1% to 74,729. The IT index surged 3.9% on Friday, taking its weekly gain to 11.7%. MSCI’s broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan fell 5.8%.

Article Title: ‘India in everybody’s plan, need to up pace’: DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan
Article Text:
DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan

TOI

Excerpts:

How is it going because of what’s happening in West Asia, what is the impact on Jebel Ali and on your revenue?

Plus, insurance…

How many trucks are you deploying to move cargo from Fujairah and other ports to Jebel Ali, 700-800? Where have you got them from?

What else did you change?

Is there a Plan C too given the attacks from the Houthis and the threat of fresh disruptions?

What does this mean for Indian cargo, you account for a large chunk of it?

There’s a change in the nature of goods being traded and electronics exports from India have grown. What is the scale of express cargo?

What is the future of IMEC? Is some preparatory work going on?

Is there a lot of congestion at ports, are containers available?

Amid global trade disruption, DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan spoke toabout his company’s plans to ensure smooth cargo movement as well as plans for India, where it is looking to invest $3-5 billion.With the Strait of Hormuz being virtually shut in terms of commercial traffic, there are few vessels coming into Jebel Ali. So, 10% of the container that we used to handle daily is what is being handled today and that too is through Khorfakkan and Fujairah. But because we are diversified, we have enough beforeJebel Ali and enough after Jebel Ali. If the Strait of Hormuz opens tomorrow, within 60 days, everybody will be back. Globally, our business is doing very well. We are not waiting but creating alternatives. We are building a new port in Fujairah, creating capacity outside the Strait of Hormuz. While there will be solutions, costs will definitely change for the worse. Today, you need roughly at least 30% more capacity on the water to handle the same cargo, globally.On top of that, the world just exited a zero-interest rate phase. As far as operating cost is concerned, double that from oil and energy consumption standpoint.If available. Before and after insurance, you need crew. You cannot put people’s lives at risk. Everybody is going to create different levels of resilience in their supply chain. It’s going to come at a significant cost and that cost is going to be ultimately paid by consumers.It will double over time. We got the trucks reasonably easily, some from Europe, some available within West Asia.We moved a lot of equipment and people from Jebel Ali to Khorfakkan. These are entry ports, we’re going to build more. Then, we opened the land bridge from Saudi, which meant we needed to get the customs authorities to work together. One of our national interests is to keep these corridors open. So, we are trying to create new links to Oman.So, you know, Europe, we are expanding capacity in Egypt, both on the port side and on the free zone side. We have a large capacity in Jeddah. We are going to open (a container terminal in) Tuna Tekra in India, which will be available by mid-next year. We are hoping Vadhvan (port) finally happens. If we were ready with Vadhvan, today it would have been used. It will enable India to provide resilient supply chains and will be essential if India has to succeed in manufacturing for the world.There’s enough capacity for the level of trade happening in India today. The success of Make in India will depend on the availability of much higher levels of capacity across the supply chain: coastal shipping, ports, roadways, rail. You need other infrastructure too. While we have seen some success, it is not happening at a scary pace, the demand is much more because people are trying to diversify away from China. India is there in everybody’s plans, but the pace has to increase.Apple has moved into India and we are pushing almost 500 tonnes of cargo a week; it can increase by 30-40%. We are bringing a lot of our global customers into India and that’s why you’ve seen our interest in FTZs, where we are doubling our capacity. We are looking to increase capacity with our inland container depot, Tuna Tekra is a big investment. We recently won a new container depot for Dadri which should be a close to Rs 2,000 crore investment. We have bid for some parts of Vadhavan. So, wherever possible, we are ready.In today’s environment, there is not much capacity, it is all lying in Jebel Ali. So, you use Fujairah and Khorfakkan, then, you use intermodal, use rail, which requires more investment. Or, once it comes to Jebel Ali, you use the Ro-Ro mechanism out ofIraq and from there to Europe by road. In fact, a vessel from India is going to do that in a week or 10 days from now.All ports are full, all the empties (containers) are stuck somewhere. A large number is stuck in the region. Global trade is very imbalanced right now. East to west is full, while half from west to east is empty (containers). Unless we get all the empties, they don’t get full. So just positioning empty containers has a huge cost.
Article Summary: DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan spoke toabout his company’s plans to ensure smooth cargo movement. He also spoke about plans for India, where it is looking to invest $3-5 billion. Narayan: The success of Make in India will depend on the availability of much higher levels of capacity across the supply chain.

Article Title: New airfare rules: Govt won’t cap charges but ensure no sudden spike in ‘exceptional’ situations
Article Text:
The new policy will require airlines to determine charges based on their “cost of operations.”

NEW DELHI: India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extra ordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.The new policy will require airlines to determine charges based on their “cost of operations.” Airlines will submit a range of fares charges on different routes to the DGCA periodically. This will help ensure no one beyond the maximum given fares.The Centre had on Friday informed the Supreme Court that administrative approval has been granted to the rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, and they are likely to be published within two weeks.“We are on the verge of finalising the new rules. However, govt will not regulate airfares in a free market, especially given the severe cost stress under which airlines are operating. We will ensure in public interest ensure under no circumstances they charge more than the highest fare bucket submitted to the regulator,” said people in the know.Govt will have the power to act in “exceptional and extra ordinary” circumstances to regulate fares for a limited period of the exigency like natural calamity when there’s a sudden demand from people to fly in or out of some place.Most recently the same was seen post the Pahalgam attack last April when almost all tourists in Kashmir wanted to fly out of Srinagar at the earliest. “This action (to regulate fares in exceptional situations) will be proportionate to the severity of the situation and be in place for only as long as required,” said sources.The DGCA will decide the periodicity in which airlines will be required to submit the range of fares to it for each route. “Airlines will share the total amount to be charged along with break-up of the same in terms of various components like base fare, taxes, surcharge and airport/user development fees of origin and destination airports. They will also share their refund policy in terms of which all components will be refunded in case of cancellations,” said sources.Instead of taking a populist route on fares, the Union aviation ministry has kept the realities of Indian airlines in which most of them are struggling to survive. The rising jet fuel prices have broken their backs. The rupee’s weakening has added to the crisis as a majority of costs like lease rentals and maintenance contracts are dollar denominated. The global geopolitical situation, especially closure of Pakistan airspace for almost 17 months now, has made things even worse.“We are all aware of airlines’ financial health. There used to be one profitable airline which is also now in the red. As long as they are not unreasonable in times of crisis, we have no intention of interfering in airfares. If anything, we are going to give them more freedom and expect them to be good samaritans in exceptional circumstances,” added sources.
Article Summary: The new policy will require airlines to determine charges based on their “cost of operations.” Airlines will submit a range of fares charges on different routes to the DGCA periodically. The Centre had on Friday informed the Supreme Court that administrative approval has been granted to the rules.

Article Title: Instant house-help race heats up as losses mount
Article Text:
Urban Company and Snabbit ramp up spending to capture instant house-help demand, as mounting losses test pricing power and growth ambitions

Bengaluru:

Urban Company is losing more money, and its chief executive Abhiraj Singh Bhal said it is choosing to do so. The company is spending heavily to become the app households turn to when their regular help takes a day off. Rival Snabbit is pursuing the same customers, with steep losses of its own. “The losses are high because we are choosing to keep them high and we are choosing to invest from a position of strength,” Bhal told analysts on Friday.Urban Company’s losses more than tripled to Rs 182.5 crore in the September quarter from Rs 59.3 crore a year earlier. Total income rose 40% to Rs 578.5 crore.Snabbit reported an Ebitda loss of Rs 145 crore for the Sept quarter in figures shared by founder Aayush Agarwal. Snabbit completed 64.5 lakh jobs, with a net transaction value of Rs 73 crore. Ebitda is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. The last two spread asset costs over time. Net loss is the final figure after all income, expenses and taxes are accounted for.Snabbit’s FY26 accounts also showed a loss of Rs 167.8 crore against Rs 5.7 crore a year earlier. Total income was Rs 27 crore, more than half coming from other income, mainly interest on bank deposits, according to regulatory filings sourced via Tofler.Agarwal offered a similar defence of spending on customer adoption, training, technology and expansion. “We made those investments deliberately, and we’d make them again,” he said. He said Snabbit’s loss per job had fallen below Rs 200 in September from about Rs 1,500 at the beginning of FY26.At InstaHelp, orders grew 63% sequentially to 62.3 lakh. Adjusted Ebitda loss widened to Rs 174 crore from Rs 132 crore in the June quarter, although loss per order fell to Rs 279 from Rs 346. Net order value declined to Rs 114 from Rs 138 amid competition and introductory offers. Urban Company’s adjusted Ebitda also excludes items such as share-based employee costs.Higher prices could test how much demand lasts. Bhal said InstaHelp would need pricing of roughly Rs 200 an hour and an average order value of Rs 300 for bookings lasting about 90 minutes. That assumes worker payouts of about Rs 150 an hour.“Once pricing fully corrects, we will see a downward correction in the orders,” he said.Urban Company’s board has approved raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through routes that could include qualified institutional placements (QIPs), subject to shareholder approval. It held Rs 1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments at September-end.“The incremental capital allows us to be more aggressive,” Bhal said. The money would support growth and potential acquisitions, although he described an acquisition in InstaHelp as “highly unlikely”.The board also approved exploring residential air conditioners under Native, its water purifier and smart lock brand. Bhal said the first one or two years would focus on learning, largely through its app.
Article Summary: Urban Company’s losses more than tripled to Rs 182.5 crore in the September quarter from Rs 59.3 crore a year earlier. Snabbit reported an Ebitda loss of Rs 145 crore for the Sept quarter in figures shared by founder Aayush Agarwal. At InstaHelp, orders grew 63% sequentially to 62.3 lakh.

Article Title: Fairfax-IDBI deal signals stronger Canada-India ties: Sidhu
Article Text:
Mumbai: Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal with Canada's Minister for International Trade Maninder Sidhu during a reception for the Team Canada trade mission to India, in Mumbai, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. (PTI Photo/Shashank Parade)(PTI10_14_2026_000578B)

Bengaluru:

Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings’ nearly $5.5 billion investment in IDBI Bank signals improving economic ties between Canada and India and could encourage further investments, Canada’s trade minister Maninder Sidhu said in Bengaluru on Friday, as the two countries work towards concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of the year.The transaction, involving the acquisition of a majority stake in IDBI Bank, will be the largest foreign investment in India’s financial sector, Sidhu said. “It’s the largest deal between our two countries in the financial sector, and that sends a clear signal to supply chains that Canada is ready to do more,” he said.Canadian pension funds and large institutions have collectively invested close to C$107 billion in India across roads, highways, healthcare, technology, clean technology and energy. Sidhu said investors were looking to expand their presence as India builds infrastructure, including highways and airports.The minister was speaking at the conclusion of a Canadian trade mission that brought around 300 business delegates representing 150 organisations to India, the largest such mission in 30 years. More than 30 deals between Canadian delegates and Indian partners, worth close to C$300 million, were concluded during the visit, he said.“When you sign a free trade agreement, the business community picks up the cues. The warming of relations between the two countries is very important,” he said.The immediate priority is CEPA, negotiations for which were relaunched in Nov last year. Five rounds have been completed, with another scheduled for the week of Nov 9 in Delhi. The agreement is expected to help more than double bilateral trade to $70 billion by 2030.Sidhu said he and commerce minister Piyush Goyal had met close to 10 times to advance negotiations. “Our goal is to conclude the agreement by the end of this year,” he said.CEPA could open up opportunities in energy, critical minerals, fertilisers, aerospace and advanced manufacturing by reducing tariffs and improving market access, Sidhu said.Citing India’s import duties of around 7-8% on potash, he said lower tariffs could make fertilisers more affordable for Indian farmers. Reduced duties on aerospace products could also bring down costs. Canada, meanwhile, has high tariffs on apparel, footwear and furniture, potentially creating opportunities for Indian exporters.“The two economies are complementary,” Sidhu said, adding that tariff lines offered clues to the sectors likely to gain most from the agreement.CEPA could also create further opportunities for Indian IT services companies in Canada, while Canadian engineering firms could contribute to India’s infrastructure development, he said.On immigration, Sidhu said Canada remained open to international students and skilled workers but wanted a more sustainable system that accounted for pressures on housing, healthcare and infrastructure.“We’re really focused on economic immigration as a government,” he said, pointing to demand for physicians and nurses in Canada’s healthcare sector. International students remained welcome, but their intake had to be sustainable, he added.
Article Summary: Fairfax Financial Holdings’ nearly $5.5 billion investment in IDBI Bank signals improving economic ties between Canada and India. Canada’s trade minister Maninder Sidhu said in Bengaluru on Friday, as the two countries work towards concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)

Article Title: IBPS SO prelims result 2026 released at ibps.in, Mains exam scheduled for November 1: Check direct link to download scorecards here
Article Text:
